html:
The Muthi Muthi, shown on the map as Madi Madi, are an Aboriginal people of southwest New South Wales, in the northern Riverina and Far West, between the lower Murrumbidgee and the Willandra Lakes.

Their country holds some of the oldest evidence of people in Australia. At Lake Mungo, now a dry lake bed, the burials of Mungo Man and Mungo Lady are around 40,000 years old. The Muthi Muthi share care of the lake and its ancestors with the Paakantyi and Ngiyampaa, and the area is a World Heritage site, the Willandra Lakes Region.

Their neighbours were the Nari Nari to the east and the Kureinji to the west. Squatters arrived in the 1840s. Mungo Man's remains were returned to the community in 2017. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
